description: This line plot illustrates the Attack Success Rate (ASR) across different datasets for three attack strategies—labeled “start,” “random,” and “end”—under a clean-label poisoning rate of 10% on the AGNews dataset. The x-axis represents distinct datasets, labeled as “s,” “bb,” “WNBA,” “ESPN,” “NHL,” “FIFA,” “Estadio,” and “athletic,” with no numerical scale or units indicated; the tick labels are spaced irregularly. The y-axis measures ASR on a linear scale ranging from 0.5 to 0.95, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The “start” strategy is represented by a teal line with circular markers and a solid line, beginning at an ASR of approximately 0.78 and ending at approximately 0.95, showing an initial decline to around 0.54 before rising sharply. The “random” strategy is depicted by an orange line with star markers and a dashed line, starting at around 0.65 and ending at approximately 0.92, with a notable dip to around 0.55. The “end” strategy is shown as a purple line with circular markers and a solid line, starting at approximately 0.77 and ending at around 0.94, exhibiting a sharp decline to approximately 0.60 before recovering to near its peak.
